responsibility: Manages cargo registration and lifecycle: creating cargo with origin, destination and arrival deadline, generating tracking identifiers, enforcing origin/destination rules, assigning selected routes to cargo, changing destinations, and flagging cargo as non-routed or requiring re-routing. Owns the cargo domain model and its consistency rules. Provides the administrative consolidated view of cargo grouped by business situation.
communicates_with: Routing Service;Location Service;Voyage Service;Handling Event Service;Cargo Tracking Service

responsibility: Computes and provides candidate routes (itineraries) compatible with a cargo's origin, destination and arrival deadline via graph traversal (pathfinder). Validates route feasibility and returns viable itineraries or signals when no option exists.

Registers logistics events (receive, load, unload, customs, claim) through multiple operational channels (operational interface, integration REST service, and periodic file/batch processing). Validates that events reference existing cargo, location and voyage, associates load/unload events with voyages, isolates invalid records for later treatment, and publishes valid events to trigger cargo status recalculation.

Recalculates and exposes the cargo transport status, last known location, next expected step, estimated arrival, route adherence and delivery history. Maintains the unified tracking model consumed by tracking, mobile and monitoring channels, distinguishing delivered, in-transit and misdirected cargo, and preserving the event history for audit.
communicates_with: Cargo Booking Service;Handling Event Service;Location Service;Voyage Service

responsibility: Manages voyages and their schedules, providing controlled lists of voyages used for routing and event registration.
Maintains the catalog of logistic locations used as controlled lists for selecting valid origins, destinations and event locations across all channels.
